opportunities.gap: Terminology drift between learner-facing support vocabulary and the backend adaptive/misconception vocabulary. The MDX 'Adaptive Support' block routes on note-type (question/confusion/insight/connection) to moves (ask-explanation/compare/transfer/show). But 03.misconceptions.json uses rail_action values explain/ask/represent/practice, and the course-wide backend policy vocabulary is explain/represent/practice/ask/advance. A learner who sees 'compare a weak and strong version' will never see a matching backend action, and the misconception 'represent'/'practice' actions have no learner-facing analogue here.
opportunities.proposed_change: Reconcile the Adaptive Support bullets (lines 135-138) with the backend rail_action set (explain/represent/practice/ask/advance). Map 'question' -> explain (already aligned), 'confusion' -> represent (the 'compare weak/strong version' bullet becomes 'show a contrasting weak/strong representation'), 'insight' -> advance (transfer to new audience), 'connection' -> represent. Either swap the MDX move verbs to the canonical set, or add one line defining the learner verbs (explain/compare/transfer/show) as surface labels for the backend actions so the two rails are explicitly linked. Confirmed in-repo: 03.misconceptions.json rail_action values are explain/ask/represent/practice only (no 'advance' and no 'compare/transfer/show'), so the divergence is real.

opportunities.gap: Terminology drift flagged at course level is present here. The learner-facing Adaptive Support block uses support moves keyed to note type: explanation→explain, confusion→compare, insight→transfer, connection→show-where. But this section's misconceptions.json rail_action vocabulary is explain / ask / represent / practice. The mapping is internally incoherent: the 'no_transfer' misconception (a confusion/ideal-only pattern) is tagged rail_action 'ask'; 'ai_supplies_vision' is tagged 'represent'; 'works_everywhere' is tagged 'practice'. These backend actions do not correspond to any move the learner-facing copy advertises, so adaptive routing cannot be explained or audited — which directly contradicts the section's own thesis that decisions must be inspectable.
opportunities.proposed_change: Reconcile the two vocabularies into one published set. Either (a) map the Adaptive Support note-type moves (explain/compare/transfer/connect) onto the rail_action field so backend and learner copy match, or (b) document the explain/represent/practice/ask/advance policy and align the learner copy to it. At minimum, fix the obviously mismatched rail_actions: 'no_transfer' should route to compare/transfer not 'ask'; 'works_everywhere' to compare not 'practice'.
